content.title: About
content.content: Cheese spread and cream cheese are soft dairy products made by curdling milk and then blending the resulting curd with additives such as butter, cream, or seasonings. They have a mild creamy flavor, a smooth texture, and are widely used as a spread, sauce ingredient, or filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cream cheese originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a cheaper alternative to traditional cottage cheese.
In Russia, the popularity of cheese spread surged in the 2010s due to the growing demand for ready‑to‑eat snacks.
Cream cheese is a key ingredient in cheesecakes, giving the filling its characteristic smoothness.
Various flavorings are added, such as herbs, smoked salmon, garlic, and pepper.
When unopened, cream cheese can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 4 weeks past the printed date.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cream cheese provides calcium, which is essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Its protein content helps maintain muscle mass and promotes satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The product contains vitamins B2 and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Low lactose content
items.content: Most lactose is removed during fermentation, making it tolerable for many people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Probiotic cultures
items.content: Some cheese spreads are fortified with live cultures that support gut microbiota.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey proteins may react to cream cheese.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Certain varieties contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Cream cheese is high in saturated fats; consumption should be moderate.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Once opened, the product loses freshness quickly; keep it sealed and respect the use‑by date.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread cheese on bread, crackers, use in sandwiches, mix into sauces, casseroles, and salads. It is often combined with herbs, spices, or smoked salmon for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the spread in the refrigerator at 2‑6 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. After opening, consume within 2‑3 weeks. Discard if it develops off‑odors, mold, or discoloration.
